sutta: 1.30 the devata said having approached you we asked a question of the slander hero with antelope carves creedless subsisting on little food wandering alone like a lion or naga without concern for essential pleasures how is one released from suffering and the buddha replied five courts of sensual pleasure in the world with mind declared to be the sixth having expunged desire here one is thus released from suffering that's the end of this so here the the devata he described the buddha as a hero with antelope carves antelope cars means the lake and the carpet is very thin you see the deer they have very thin calves subsisting on little food wandering alone like a lion or naga naga here refers to a big elephant now or a big serpent so he's asking the buddha he considers the buddha a great hero that means sights sounds smells taste and touch all these are that give us pleasure in the world we have to cut off desire for it and also the mind the mind also gives us the sixth type of pleasure we cut off and then oniya we can be released from suffering
